In recent years, nanodelivery platforms such as liposomes, polymeric nanoparticles, exosomes, and metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) have been proven to markedly enhance EGCG stability, brain-targeted delivery efficiency, and overall bioavailability. These nanocarriers exert enhanced neuroprotective effects and confer synergistic therapeutic benefits when combined with standard agents such as nimodipine in experimental stroke models, offering novel strategies to overcome the translational bottlenecks of free EGCG. This review systematically summarizes research advances in EGCG's multi-target neuroprotective mechanisms, nanocarrier delivery systems, and translational prospects, focusing on analyzing the strengths and limitations of existing evidence and identifying future research directions. Future investigations should prioritize optimizing brain-targeted delivery platforms, standardizing pharmacokinetic evaluation, unifying therapeutic dose specifications, and conducting high-quality randomized controlled trials to accelerate the clinical transformation of EGCG nanoformulations for precision stroke therapy.

articles.title: From molecular correction to functional rescue: delivery, tissue state, and immunobiology as the principal constraints on dystrophin-restoring therapy in Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
articles.abstract: Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) arises from thousands of distinct mutations at a single X-linked locus that converge on loss of functional dystrophin, and this convergence on one molecular endpoint-rather than any genetic uniformity-has long made the disease appear a candidate for straightforward molecular correction. Three decades of work indicate that the difficulty lies less in restoring dystrophin than in restoring it adequately along four axes: amount, retained domains, breadth of coverage across skeletal muscle, diaphragm, heart and brain-the constraint being extent of coverage rather than correctness of sarcolemmal localization, which these platforms achieve reliably-and persistence in regenerating tissue. We argue that DMD is best understood as a systemic delivery problem superimposed on a progressive regenerative disorder, in which cargo design, biodistribution, cardiac coverage, immune response, disease stage and endpoint design jointly determine clinical benefit. AAV-microdystrophin has shown that body-wide expression is achievable, but delivers a truncated protein from an episomal genome at a dose whose upper bound was set by toxicity in other indications and whose minimum effective value was established in mdx mice rather than titrated in patients, leaving the therapeutic window better defined at its toxic than at its lower boundary. Exon skipping establishes that low-magnitude restoration is not trivial; genome editing addresses durability but adds integration risk; non-viral carriers permit redosing yet lack the potency required for a compartment comprising a third of body mass. Immunobiology constrains the field at several sequential levels, each now partially modifiable. Because the immunological burden of body-wide delivery can itself limit benefit, safety and efficacy are not fully separable, and progress is better judged by corrected muscle mass relative to immunological burden than by peak biopsy expression.

articles.title: Agomelatine improves symptom severity and quality of life in diarrhea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome: insights from a randomized controlled clinical trial.
articles.abstract: Irritable bowel syndrome with diarrhea predominance (IBS-D) significantly impairs Quality of Life (QOL) and is often accompanied by psychological distress. Agomelatine, a melatonergic antidepressant, has shown promise in modulating gastrointestinal symptoms and mood disorders. This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of agomelatine in patients with IBS-D. In this 8-week, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial, 61 adults aged 18-65 years with IBS-D diagnosed by Rome IV criteria and confirmed normal colonic anatomy and labs were randomized to agomelatine (12.5 mg daily, titrated to 25 mg) or placebo. Baseline symptoms were recorded during a 1-week run-in using the Bristol Stool Form Scale (BSFS) and IBS Symptom Severity Score (IBS-SSS). Psychological status was assessed using the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale-Anxiety (HADS-A) and Depression (HADS-D) subscales, and QOL by the IBS Quality of Life questionnaire (IBS-QOL). The primary outcome was change in total IBS-SSS from baseline to week 8. Secondary outcomes included changes in individual IBS-SSS domains, stool consistency, bowel movement frequency, symptom days (pain, diarrhea, urgency, bloating), HADS-A, HADS-D, and IBS-QOL scores. Safety was monitored via adverse events and treatment discontinuations. All randomized participants were included in the intention-to-treat analysis. Both groups showed significant within-group reductions in total IBS-SSS (p < 0.001). Agomelatine produced greater reductions in total IBS-SSS than placebo (between-group difference in mean change, - 24.80 points; p = 0.034), abdominal pain severity, and abdominal pain frequency. The week-8 interference-with-life score was lower with agomelatine than with placebo, although the between-group difference in change from baseline was not statistically significant. The responder rate, defined as a reduction of at least 50 points in total IBS-SSS, was higher with agomelatine than with placebo (67.7% vs. 33.3%; p = 0.007). Daily bowel-movement frequency and days with pain, diarrhea, and urgency decreased significantly more with agomelatine (all p < 0.05). Anxiety and depression scores decreased, and IBS-QOL improved, significantly more with agomelatine than with placebo (all p ≤ 0.001). Adverse events were more frequent with agomelatine than placebo (61.3% vs. 23.3%; p = 0.004) and were predominantly mild to moderate. Two participants in the agomelatine group discontinued treatment because of adverse events, compared with none in the placebo group; no serious adverse events were reported. Agomelatine effectively improves gastrointestinal symptoms, psychological distress, and QOL in IBS-D patients and is generally well tolerated, supporting its therapeutic potential.Trial registration: The trial was registered at Iranian Registry of Clinical Trials ( https://irct.behdasht.gov.ir/trial/80432 ) (ID code: IRCT20120215009014N544) on November 30, 2024.

articles.title: Formononetin attenuates ethanol-induced gastric ulcer injury by targeting ALDH2 to inhibit oxidative stress.
articles.abstract: Ethanol-induced gastric ulceration is primarily driven by oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and gastric epithelial cell injury. Although formononetin (Fmn), a naturally occurring isoflavone, possesses well-documented antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties, its protective role and underlying molecular mechanisms in ethanol-induced gastric injury remain unclear. In this study, ethanol-treated GES-1 gastric epithelial cells were used as an in vitro model to investigate the cytoprotective effects of Fmn. Cell proliferation, apoptosis, oxidative stress, and mitochondrial function were evaluated using biochemical and cellular assays. Potential molecular targets were identified through SwissTargetPrediction and molecular docking, followed by experimental validation, including ALDH2 knockdown, qRT-PCR, and enzymatic activity assays. Fmn significantly attenuated ethanol-induced cellular injury by restoring cell proliferation, suppressing apoptosis, reducing intracellular and mitochondrial reactive oxygen species, decreasing malondialdehyde levels, and enhancing superoxide dismutase activity. Molecular docking demonstrated a strong binding affinity between Fmn and aldehyde dehydrogenase 2 (ALDH2), which was further confirmed by increased ALDH2 mRNA and protein expression as well as enhanced enzymatic activity following Fmn treatment. Functional studies revealed that ALDH2 upregulation plays a pivotal role in preserving mitochondrial integrity and limiting oxidative damage. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that Fmn protects gastric epithelial cells against ethanol-induced injury through ALDH2-mediated suppression of oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction, highlighting its potential as a promising therapeutic candidate for the prevention and treatment of alcohol-induced gastric ulceration.

articles.title: Neuroprotective Effects of Bauhinia variegata Flower Extract against D-Galactose-Induced Age-Related Cognitive Impairment: Modulation of the Oxidative Stress-endoplasmic reticulum Axis.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Bauhinia variegata is widely used in traditional medicine for the management of disorders associated with inflammation, oxidative stress, and nervous system dysfunction. The presence of flavonoids and phenolics supports its ethnopharmacological relevance to cognitive impairment, both reported to exert neuroprotective, antioxidant, and cholinesterase-inhibitory activities AIM OF THE STUDY: The present study investigated the neuroprotective potential of B. variegata flower ethanolic extract (BV-EtOH) against D-galactose (D-Gal)-induced age-related cognitive impairment in rats, with emphasis on its anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and anti-tauopathic mechanisms. RESULTS: Chronic D-Gal administration (120 mg/kg) for 8 consecutive weeks induced significant oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, and cognitive impairment, whereas BV-EtOH treatment (50, 100, and 200 mg/kg, p.o., 8 weeks) markedly reversed these alterations. BV-EtOH improved learning and memory by reducing escape latency in the Morris Water Maze by 56.3% and increasing target quadrant time by 48.7% (p < 0.01), while the Object Recognition Test showed a 61.4% rise in discrimination index. Biochemically, BV-EtOH restored GSH levels (74.2%) and reduced MDA (63.5%), alongside significant down regulation of TNF-α (52.8%), IL-1β (47.9%), NF-κB (45.6%), and Endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress mediators GRP78, CHOP, and P-PERK (58-67%) (p < 0.001). Notably, p-Tau expression decreased by 54.1% with concurrent inhibition of GSK-3β, while BDNF and NeuN increased by 2.3- and 2.7-fold, respectively, indicating enhanced neurogenesis and synaptic integrity. UPLC-ESI-MS/MS analysis identified 133 bioactive compounds, mainly flavonoids, phenolic acids, proanthocyanidins, and coumarins, collectively contributing to the extract's multitarget modulation of oxidative, inflammatory, ER stress, and tau phosphorylation pathways. CONCLUSION: These findings demonstrate that BV-EtOH exerts potent neuroprotective efficacy and holds therapeutic promise for the prevention and management of neuroinflammatory and neurodegenerative disorders.

articles.title: Defining a comprehensive set of value assessment criteria for funders of drug repurposing initiatives.
articles.abstract: AIMS: This study aims to develop a structured list of value assessment criteria for drug repurposing (DR) projects designed to support consistent, evidence-informed decision-making by funders. The assessment criteria were developed within the REMEDi4ALL project, a multi-stakeholder Horizon Europe funded initiative to advance DR and were validated through consultation with public and philanthropic funding organizations. METHODS: Relevant assessment criteria were identified through a review of organizational documents and stakeholder consultations and were further supplemented by a targeted literature search in PubMed and Google Scholar. RESULTS: A total of 330 candidate criteria were identified from funder documentation and peer-reviewed literature. Following internal review and consultation with additional REMEDi4ALL partner organizations, 37 assessment criteria were defined and organized into five domains: basic enablers, expected benefits, technical implementation, business opportunity and fundraising profile. Each criterion was assigned a clear, standardized definition to ensure consistent interpretation and application. CONCLUSIONS: This study presents a transparent, adaptable and non-proprietary set of value assessment criteria to support the evaluation of DR proposals. It addresses key methodological and applicability gaps by enabling funders to apply structured assessments that reflect diverse value perspectives and stages of development in standalone or joint funding settings. The criteria list is clearly defined and grouped into five domains that also serves as the core for further application. The list has already been implemented in an Excel-based application to select, weight and score items based on funder's strategic priorities and project maturity. It is freely available through the REMEDi4ALL platform.

articles.title: Assessing the Influence of CYP3A4 Inhibitors on Voriconazole Exposure across CYP2C19 Genotypes: A Physiologically Based Pharmacokinetic Model Analysis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Voriconazole (VCZ) is a triazole antifungal agent used to treat invasive infections. It has narrow therapeutic index and exhibits high interindividual variability due to cytochrome P450 (CYP) 3A4 autoinhibition and CYP2C19 polymorphism. As VCZ is a CYP3A4 substrate, it is susceptible to drug-drug interactions (DDIs) with CYP3A4 inhibitors, resulting in increased VCZ exposure. However, due to the differences in CYP2C19 activity, the fraction of VCZ metabolized by CYP3A4 varies across CYP2C19 genotypes. As a result, coadministration of CYP3A4 inhibitors could result in genotype-dependent increases in VCZ exposure, leading to a disproportionate risk for toxicity across genotypes. Despite this, the clinical impact of CYP3A4 inhibition on VCZ exposure across different CYP2C19 genotypes remains poorly characterized. OBJECTIVE: The purpose of this study was to develop a genotype-specific VCZ physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) model to assess the impact of CYP3A4 inhibition and CYP2C19 polymorphism on VCZ exposure. METHODS: A genotype-specific VCZ PBPK model was developed and evaluated in PK-Sim® using observed VCZ pharmacokinetic and DDI data. VCZ-CYP3A4 inhibitor DDI potential was assessed by comparing model predicted VCZ exposure with or without CYP3A4 inhibitors across CYP2C19 genotypes. Due to VCZ's CYP3A4 autoinhibition, DDI potential was assessed following single doses of VCZ and at steady state. Furthermore, the risk of toxicity was determined by estimating the percentage of virtual individuals with VCZ trough concentrations (Ctrough) exceeding 5.5 mg/L, a toxic threshold associated with serious adverse events such as neurotoxicity. RESULTS: Model simulations with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor (clarithromycin) across CYP2C19 genotypes demonstrated greater relative increases in VCZ exposure after a single dose compared with steady state. Following clarithromycin coadministration, a genotype-dependent increase in single-dose VCZ exposure (relative to VCZ alone) was found, with geometric mean fold increases of 1.57, 1.78, 2.31, and 3.24 in extensive, normal, intermediate, and poor metabolizers, respectively. However, steady-state increases in VCZ exposure with clarithromycin were minimal and similar across CYP2C19 genotypes: 1.40-fold in extensive, 1.60-fold in normal, 1.41-fold in intermediate, and 1.26-fold in poor metabolizers. In the absence or presence of clarithromycin, model-predicted single-dose Ctrough levels did not exceed the toxic threshold in any genotype. In contrast, compared with VCZ alone, clarithromycin coadministration increased the percentage of virtual individuals with steady-state Ctrough levels beyond the toxic threshold. This increased from 2 to 11% in normal, 24 to 50% in intermediate, and 63 to 87% in poor metabolizers, while no meaningful change was exhibited in extensive metabolizers (0 to 0%). CONCLUSIONS: Overall, this analysis demonstrates the capacity of PBPK modeling to predict DDIs across different genotypes and dosing scenarios. Although the relative increase in steady-state VCZ exposure was predicted to be similar across genotypes, this analysis demonstrated that CYP2C19 intermediate and poor metabolizers are at elevated risk of VCZ toxicity in the presence of strong CYP3A4 inhibition.

articles.title: Hippo-YAP signaling: A novel pathway regulating platelet activation and thrombogenesis.
articles.abstract: AIM: To investigate the functional significance of Hippo-YAP signaling in platelet activation and thrombosis. METHODS: Expression and phosphorylation of YAP were examined in platelets exposed to physiological agonists as well as mechanical cues (adhesion to matrices having varying stiffness and activation of mechanosensitive channel Piezo1). Involvements of LATS kinase and RhoA-ROCK-actomyosin axis in YAP signaling were evaluated. Effect of pharmacological inhibition of YAP on platelet activation parameters (αIIbβ3 activation, adhesion, α-granule secretion, extracellular vesicle release, and fibrin clot retraction) were studied ex vivo. Contribution of YAP to pathological thrombosis was further investigated in a murine model in vivo. YAP activity was also assessed in platelets obtained from patients diagnosed with acute coronary syndrome. KEY FINDINGS: Platelets expressed mRNA transcript as well as peptide of YAP, whose phosphorylation (at Ser-127) was modulated in response to physiological agonists and mechanical stimuli. Adhesion to immobilized matrix, Piezo1 stimulation, and exposure to agonists markedly enhanced YAP expression. Concomitantly, these factors prompted dephosphorylation of YAP, suggestive of YAP functional impairment, driven by the upstream LATS kinase and RhoA-ROCK-actomyosin signaling axis. Inhibition of YAP impaired key platelet functions ex vivo, that included integrin αIIbβ3 activation, adhesion, α-granule secretion, extracellular vesicle release, and fibrin clot retraction, and exerted marked protection against pathological thrombosis in a murine model in vivo. Consistent with above, platelets obtained from patients diagnosed with acute coronary syndrome were found to harbour enhanced YAP activity. CONCLUSION: These findings underscore a contributing role of YAP in thrombogenesis, highlighting its potential as an antiplatelet therapeutic target.

articles.title: Combined erythropoietin and sodium butyrate ameliorate imiquimod-induced lupus-like autoimmunity in mice through modulation of inflammatory and interferon-associated responses.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a complex autoimmune disorder characterized by systemic inflammation and multi-organ damage. Current therapeutic options remain limited and are associated with significant side effects. This study investigated the immunomodulatory and anti-inflammatory effects of Erythropoietin (EPO) and sodium butyrate (NaB), as individual and combined interventions, in a Balb/C mice model of imiquimod (IMQ)-induced lupus-like autoimmunity. METHODS: Fifty female Balb/C mice were randomly assigned into five equal groups: normal control, IMQ-untreated SLE, EPO-treated, NaB-treated, and EPO + NaB-treated SLE group. We evaluated the systemic response via body weight changes and splenic index. Immunological and biochemical profiles were assessed through anti-dsDNA antibodies, creatinine levels, and proteinuria. To elucidate the underlying mechanism, we analyzed renal Myxovirus resistance protein 1 (MX1) gene expression (an interferon-regulated marker), interleukin-6 (IL-6) levels, and the immunohistochemical expression of nuclear factor-κB (NF-κB). Histopathological changes in skin and kidney tissues were examined using hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) and Periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) staining. RESULTS: Combined treatment demonstrated superior efficacy compared to monotherapies. These effects were associated with significant amelioration in body weight, reduction in the splenic index, reduced MX1 expression, and NF-κB suppression, leading to a marked decrease in IL-6, anti-dsDNA antibodies, and creatinine levels. Histopathological analysis confirmed that the combination therapy effectively preserved renal architecture and attenuated skin lesions. CONCLUSION: EPO and NaB may exert a potent protective effect against SLE-induced damage. These effects were associated with modulation of inflammatory and interferon-associated responses.

articles.title: Paeonol alleviates oxidative stress and brain injury in hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy by activating the PI3K/Akt/Nrf2 signaling pathway.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Hypoxic-Ischemic Encephalopathy (HIE) is a severe neonatal neurological disorder, in which oxidative stress serves as a central mediator of brain injury. Paeonol (Pae), a phenolic compound with established anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, remains underexplored as a therapeutic strategy for HIE. This study investigated the neuroprotective effects of Pae against HIE-induced brain injury and explored whether its protective effects involves attenuation of oxidative stress through activation of the PI3K/Akt/Nrf2 signaling pathway. METHODS: A neonatal rat HIE model was established using the modified Rice-Vannucci method. Brain injury, oxidative stress markers, and neurological function were assessed through histological staining and behavioral testing. Network pharmacology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations were used to identify and validate potential targets. An H2O2-induced oxidative stress model in PC12 cells was employed for mechanistic validation, with PI3K and Nrf2 pharmacologically inhibited using LY294002 and ML385, respectively. RESULTS: Pae significantly reduced cerebral infarct volume and histopathological alterations, attenuated oxidative stress, and improved motor and cognitive performance in HIE rats. Network pharmacology identified the PI3K/Akt as a key target pathway, while molecular docking revealed a strong binding affinity between Pae and AKT1. Consistently, Pae activated the PI3K/Akt pathway, promoted Nrf2 nuclear translocation, and upregulated HO-1 expression in both in vivo and in vitro experiments; these effects were substantially reversed by LY294002 and ML385. CONCLUSION: Pae ameliorates HIE-induced brain injury and neurological deficits via activation of the PI3K-Akt signaling pathway and reinforcement of Nrf2-mediated antioxidant defenses. These findings identify Pae as a preclinical neuroprotective candidate worthy of further exploration.

articles.title: circ_0029343 promotes malignant phenotypes in clear cell renal cell carcinoma and is associated with miR-490-5p/NAT10 signaling and pyroptosis-related pathways.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) is a highly metastatic and aggressive form of kidney cancer with limited treatment options and poor patient outcomes. CircRNAs are key regulators in tumor development, but the specific function of circ_0029343 in ccRCC has not been fully elucidated. The objective of this study was to determine the functional significance and regulatory pathways of circ_0029343 in ccRCC. METHODS: The expression of Circ_0029343 was examined in ccRCC tissues and cells using qRT-PCR assay. To validate circ_0029343 as a circular RNA, we confirmed the back-splice junction, assessed RNase R resistance and transcript stability, and determined subcellular localization. Clinical associations were evaluated using chi-square tests, univariate and multivariable logistic regression for postoperative recurrence/metastasis, and a nomogram model with bootstrap calibration and ROC/AUC assessment. Functional assays, including Cell Counting Kit-8 (CCK-8), Transwell invasion, and immunofluorescence staining, were performed to assess the effects of Circ_0029343 knockdown on proliferation, invasion, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT). Dual-luciferase and RNA pull-down assays were conducted to confirm the interaction between Circ_0029343 and miR-490-5p. The downstream target of miR-490-5p, NAT10, was validated through bioinformatics and functional analyses. The impact of circ_0029343 on pyroptosis-associated signaling was assessed by measuring NLRP3, cleaved caspase-1, IL-1β, and gasdermin D (GSDMD-N) expression levels, LDH release, and phase-contrast microscopy to evaluate pyroptosis-like lytic cell death characteristics. Additional evaluation of inflammasome/caspase-1-dependent activation of the caspase-1/GSDMD axis involved caspase-1 inhibition rescue (VX-765) and time-course analyses of cleaved caspase-1 and GSDMD-N. A xenograft model was utilized to assess tumor growth in vivo. RESULTS: High circ_0029343 expression was also associated with postoperative recurrence/metastasis risk, and a multivariable logistic regression-based nomogram demonstrated good discrimination (AUC = 0.835) with satisfactory calibration. Circ_0029343 exhibited a back-splice junction, RNase R resistance, greater stability than linear SCARB1 transcripts, and cytoplasmic localization. Knockdown of circ_0029343 suppressed proliferation, invasion, and EMT, while promoting pyroptosis-associated signaling and lytic cell death characteristics indicative of pyroptosis, demonstrated by heightened LDH release, activation of the NLRP3/caspase-1/GSDMD pathway, and pyroptosis-like morphology. In vitro, circ_0029343 functioned as a ceRNA for miR-490-5p, correlating with elevated NAT10 levels, thus implicating the miR-490-5p/NAT10 axis in malignant characteristics. In a Caki-1 subcutaneous xenograft model, circ_0029343 knockdown decreased tumor growth and was accompanied by changes in miR-490-5p/NAT10 and pyroptosis-related markers. CONCLUSIONS: Circ_0029343 promotes ccRCC malignant phenotypes and is associated with pyroptosis-related signaling; in vitro data support that circ_0029343 may exert these effects, at least in part, through miR-490-5p/NAT10 signaling.

articles.title: COL11A1 accumulation in the zona pellucida is associated with morphological severity of agar-like zona pellucida in human oocytes.
articles.abstract: Agar-like zona pellucida (AZP) is a rare abnormality of the zona pellucida (ZP) characterized by a compact, homogeneous matrix and a markedly narrowed or absent perivitelline space. In this study, we integrated clinical phenotyping, ultrastructural analysis, single-oocyte RNA sequencing, immunofluorescence, and collagenase treatment to investigate molecular features associated with AZP severity. Immunofluorescence showed no obvious loss or redistribution of the canonical ZP glycoproteins ZP1-ZP4, whereas ultrastructural analysis revealed marked matrix compaction and disorganization. Single-oocyte RNA sequencing identified COL11A1 as a prominently upregulated candidate gene in AZP oocytes. At the protein level, COL11A1 accumulated within the ZP, and stronger COL11A1 signals were observed with increasing morphological severity from mild to typical AZP. In a limited number of AZP oocytes, collagenase treatment produced partial re-expansion of the perivitelline space and reduced ZP compactness, indicating a partial morphological response. Collectively, these findings identify COL11A1 upregulation and ZP-associated COL11A1 accumulation as prominent molecular features of AZP and suggest that COL11A1 accumulation is associated with morphological severity. Further studies are required to determine whether COL11A1 contributes causally to ZP remodeling and whether it can serve as a reliable severity-associated biomarker.

articles.title: Celastrol attenuates testosterone-induced benign prostatic hyperplasia by modulating the PTEN/PI3K/AKT pathway.
articles.abstract: Benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) represents a prevalent urological disease observed primarily among aging men. Celastrol (CELA) is an active natural compound with diverse pharmacological properties. The primary aim of this research is to assess the potential protective activity of CELA in testosterone (TEST)-induced BPH in rats. Male Wistar rats were allocated into six distinct groups for treatment: group 1 acted as the control and was given the vehicle; group 2 received only CELA (2 mg/kg, orally); group 3 was administered TEST alone (3 mg/kg, subcutaneously); groups 4 and 5 were administered the combination of TEST (3 mg/kg, subcutaneously) and CELA (1 or 2 mg/kg, orally); and group 6 received a combination of TEST (3 mg/kg, subcutaneously) and finasteride (FINA) (0.5 mg/kg, orally). Over a period of four weeks, CELA at doses of 1 or 2 mg/kg effectively inhibited the increase in both the prostate index and weight when compared to rats treated with TEST. CELA mitigated pathological alterations in prostate architecture, reduced the proliferation markers and modulated the expression of apoptosis markers compared to TEST-treated rats. Furthermore, CELA exhibited antioxidant properties by mitigating the TEST-induced increase in lipid peroxide levels and the depletion of superoxide dismutase and catalase activities. Moreover, CELA exhibited anti-inflammatory activity by significantly downregulating tumor necrosis factor-α, interleukin-6, and nuclear factor-κB expression. In addition, CELA elevated phosphatase and tensin homolog (PTEN) and reduced phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K) and AKT expression compared with the TEST group. In addition, CELA inhibited TEST-induced enhancement of mRNA expression of 5α-reductase type 2, androgen receptor and fibroblast growth factor 2. Overall, CELA partially alleviates TEST-induced BPH in rats, an effect that is associated with modulation of PTEN/PI3K/AKT axis.

articles.title: Beyond Efficacy, Integrated toxicological profiling reveals the preclinical safety of Berberis lycium Royle and its principal alkaloid, Berberine.
articles.abstract: Berberis lycium Royle has been widely used in traditional medicine for the treatment of infectious, inflammatory, gastrointestinal, and metabolic disorders. Berberine, its principal isoquinoline alkaloid, is considered an important bioactive constituent associated with several of its pharmacological effects. Despite its ethnomedicinal use, further toxicological assessment is needed to characterize the safety of the crude extract and berberine under defined experimental conditions. The present study evaluated the acute oral toxicity of the crude methanolic extract (CME) of Berberis lycium root bark and berberine in Wistar rats, and investigated the concentration-dependent effects of berberine on the viability of human embryonic kidney cells (HEK-293). Acute oral toxicity was assessed according to OECD Test Guideline 425. Male and female Wistar rats received oral administration of CME (300 mg/kg body weight) or berberine (100 mg/kg body weight). Clinical observations, body weight, food and water consumption, haematological parameters, and serum biochemical markers of hepatic, renal, and metabolic function were evaluated. The in-vitro effects of berberine were assessed using the MTT assay following 24 h exposure of HEK-293 cells to concentrations ranging from 0 to 100 μM. Neither berberine nor CME produced mortality or clinically significant signs of toxicity during the observation period. The oral LD50 of both preparations was reported to exceed 2000 mg/kg body weight. Body weight gain, feed intake, water consumption, haematological indices, and biochemical parameters remained comparable to untreated controls. Berberine produced a concentration-dependent reduction in HEK-293 cell viability, with a marked decline observed up to 40 μM, after which the response approached saturation. Under the conditions tested, CME and berberine were well tolerated in the acute oral toxicity assessment in Wistar rats, while berberine showed concentration-dependent effects on HEK-293 cell viability in vitro. These findings provide evidence regarding acute oral safety at the tested doses, but do not establish overall preclinical safety. The assessment was limited to acute exposure and selected in-vivo endpoints, alongside an in-vitro MTT assay; therefore, it does not address potential effects of repeated or long-term exposure, reproductive toxicity, or other unexamined toxicological outcomes. Further repeated-dose, chronic, reproductive, and mechanistic studies are required to more fully characterize their safety.

articles.title: Tongmai Yizhi Decoction Improves Post-Stroke Cognitive Impairment by Inhibiting Monoamine Oxidase to Reduce Dopamine Metabolism.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Tongmai Yizhi Decoction (TMYZD), a classic Chinese ethnomedical formula derived from Danggui Shaoyao San and Shenghui Decoction, has long been used for post-stroke amnesia and dementia as it activates blood circulation, tonifies kidney essence, resolves phlegm, and opens cerebral orifices. Its clinical efficacy against post-stroke cognitive impairment (PSCI) is verified, but the underlying pharmacological mechanisms remain unclear. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to investigate the protective effect of TMYZD against PSCI and verify whether it acts via modulating the dopamine metabolic pathway to elucidate its molecular targets and pharmacological basis. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Network pharmacology was applied to predict therapeutic targets, and metabolomics combined with mass spectrometry was used to identify regulated pathways. In vivo, middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion rats were assessed for cognitive function, synaptic ultrastructure, and key target proteins. In vitro, HT22 cells under oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation with monoamine oxidase-B (MAOB) overexpression were used for target validation. RESULTS: PSCI rats exhibited severe cognitive decline and synaptic structural damage. Monoamine oxidase-A (MAOA) and MAOB were identified as core therapeutic targets. TMYZD significantly regulated the dopamine pathway, upregulated tyrosine hydroxylase and dopamine receptor D2, downregulated MAOA/MAOB, and ameliorated synaptic injury. MAOB overexpression partially abolished the neuroprotective effect of TMYZD, confirming MAOB as a key target. CONCLUSIONS: TMYZD improves cognitive function in PSCI by regulating dopamine metabolism, elevating dopamine levels, and enhancing synaptic plasticity, with MAOB as a critical target. These findings provide scientific evidence for the ethnomedical application of TMYZD in PSCI.

articles.title: Bioactivity-guided identification of antithrombotic peptides from an ethanol-soluble fraction of Hirudo nipponia with anticoagulant and antiplatelet activities.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Medicinal leeches have long been administered orally in traditional Chinese medicine for blood stasis-related disorders. The thermal instability and poor oral bioavailability of hirudin suggest that other heat- and digestion-resistant constituents may contribute to the pharmacological activity of orally administered leech preparations. AIM OF THE STUDY: To characterize the antithrombotic activity of an ethanol-soluble fraction derived from processed Hirudo nipponia decoction pieces (Hn70) and identify peptide candidates with anticoagulant and antiplatelet activities. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Hn70 was prepared by aqueous extraction followed by 70% ethanol fractionation. Its anticoagulant and antiplatelet activities, in vivo antithrombotic effects, and retention of anticoagulant activity under thermal and simulated gastrointestinal conditions were evaluated. Antithrombin activity was quantified using recombinant hirudin as an activity reference. The major active fraction was isolated by bioactivity-guided gel filtration, followed by coagulation factor and platelet aggregation assays, nLC-MS/MS-based de novo sequencing, bioinformatics screening, molecular docking, and functional validation of selected peptides. RESULTS: Hn70 showed concentration-dependent anticoagulant and antiplatelet activities and significantly reduced carrageenan-induced thrombosis in vivo. Six batches showed a specific antithrombin activity of 1.156 ± 0.020 ATU·mg-1 dry Hn70 (CV, 1.70%). Hn70 retained substantial anticoagulant activity after thermal and simulated gastrointestinal treatment. Hn70-D was identified as a major active fraction that reduced multiple coagulation-factor activities and inhibited platelet aggregation. Twenty-eight peptides were identified, and seven selected synthetic peptides exhibited both activities in single-concentration assays. CONCLUSION: Hn70 is an antithrombotic fraction of Hirudo nipponia that retains substantial anticoagulant activity after thermal treatment and simulated gastrointestinal digestion. Bioactivity-guided analysis identified Hn70-D and candidate peptides for further investigation of its antithrombotic pharmacology.

articles.title: Biotransformation and metabolite formation of lavender (Lavandula officinalis) flower infusion by human gut microbiota.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Lavandula officinalis has been traditionally used for its calming, digestive, and antimicrobial properties. Historically, its flowers were employed in baths, perfumes, medicinal preparations, and as a mild laxative. Today, lavender infusions are widely consumed in beverages and functional foods for their aroma and potential health benefits. Despite its popularity, little is known about how lavender infusions interact with human gut microbiota and influence the biotransformation of their polyphenolic compounds. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to chemically characterize a commercially available lavender flower infusion and to investigate its interaction with human gut microbiota in an ex vivo setting, focusing on polyphenol biotransformation and changes in microbial composition. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The lavender extract was incubated with the human gut microbiota from six healthy donors. The composition of the extract and the identification of metabolites following incubation with ex vivo gut microbiota were conducted using UHPLC-DAD-IT-MS. Quantitative analysis of Z-melilotoside and Z-4-methoxymelilotoside was performed by HPLC-DAD using a Shimadzu system. The principal compounds isolated by preparative HPLC were identified based on their NMR spectra. Bacterial genomic DNA was extracted and examined by amplification sequencing of the 16S rDNA to determine changes in bacterial composition. RESULTS: The UHPLC-DAD-IT-MS identified 31 polyphenolic compounds, including hydroxycinnamic acid derivatives and flavonoid glycosides, several of which have been reported for the first time in lavender. Ex vivo incubation revealed microbial metabolism producing coumarin, herniarin, E-o-coumaric acid, E-4-methoxy-o-coumaric acid, luteolin, and apigenin. Quantitative analysis showed that a 250 mL serving of LOI contained 24.88 ± 1.41 mg of Z-melilotoside and 24.26 ± 1.77 mg of Z-4-methoxymelilotoside, corresponding to estimated coumarin and herniarin yields of 11.15 ± 0.63 mg and 11.99 ± 0.79 mg, respectively, assuming complete conversion. LOI treatment was not associated with major alterations in the overall microbial community structure and was associated with changes in the relative abundance of taxa, including Faecalibacterium, Prevotella, and Mediterraneibacter. CONCLUSION: Lavender flower infusion is extensively transformed by the human gut microbiota, forming metabolites with potential biological relevance. Assuming complete conversion, the estimated coumarin exposure from a 250 mL serving of the infusion would be approximately 1.9-fold higher than the tolerable daily intake for a 60 kg adult. For herniarin, no tolerable daily intake has been established, highlighting the need for further studies on its safety.

articles.title: Aqueous Hellenia speciosa rhizome extract attenuates hepatic injury in high-fat diet/streptozotocin-induced diabetic rats.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Rhizomes of Hellenia speciosa (J.Koenig) S.R.Dutta (Costaceae), used in Ayurvedic and folk medicine as Costus speciosus for diabetes and jaundice, remain underexplored. No chemically characterised aqueous preparation has been evaluated against a clinical comparator in diabetes-associated hepatic injury. AIM OF THE STUDY: To test whether an aqueous H. speciosa rhizome extract (CS-AE) is associated with attenuated hepatic injury in high-fat diet (HFD)/streptozotocin (STZ) diabetic male rats, and to benchmark it against metformin (MET). MATERIALS AND METHODS: Wistar rats were randomised into six groups (n = 10): normal control (NC), NC + CS-AE, diabetic control (DC), and DC receiving MET (200 mg/kg/day), CS-AE (500 mg/kg/day) or both, orally for six weeks. This single CS-AE dose is 4.5-9 times the pharmacopoeial dose. Endpoints included metabolic and hepatic biochemistry, oxidative stress, mitochondrial function, protein/gene expression and histopathology. CS-AE was characterised in-house by an ICH Q2(R2)-validated HPLC-DAD method against four markers at Schymanski Level 3. RESULTS: Versus DC, CS-AE was associated with reduced fasting glucose (218 vs. 310 mg/dL), HOMA-IR (24.0 vs. 58.3), ALT (48 vs. 91 U/L) and malondialdehyde (3.1 vs. 4.4 nmol/mg protein; all p < 0.001). CS-AE showed larger Nrf2/HO-1/NQO1 changes than MET, whereas MET showed lower glucose and higher p-AMPKα. The combination gave the most favourable profile. CONCLUSIONS: At this supra-traditional dose, CS-AE was associated with attenuated diabetic hepatic injury; its profile complemented metformin's. Findings are association-level. Dose-response studies that include the traditional dose, and causal, pharmacokinetic, sex-inclusive and clinical studies, are required before any therapeutic recommendation.

articles.title: Ethnopharmacological relevance of Aristolochia paucinervis leaf: phytochemical profile and assessment of wound healing, antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Aristolochia paucinervis Pomel is a perennial Western Mediterranean plant, traditionally used to treat wounds, inflammation, snakebites, skin diseases, cancer, infections, and pain. Despite its extensive use, studies on its phytochemistry, pharmacological properties, and safety remains limited. AIM: This study provides the first phytochemical characterisation of A. paucinervis leaf decoction and evaluates its total phenolic content, as well as its antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and wound-healing potential, and safety profile. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A decoction from A. paucinervis leaf was prepared according to traditional practices. Its phytochemical profile was characterized by HPLC-PDA-MSn and TLC, quantified using HPLC-PDA, and total phenolic content assessed by Folin-Ciocalteau. Antioxidant potential was assessed using in vitro chemical assays (DPPH, ABTS, and FRAP). Anti-inflammatory activity and safety were preliminary assessed in RAW 264.7 macrophages, by NO and resazurin assays, respectively. Wound-healing potential and safety were determined using the scratch wound assay in NIH/3T3 fibroblasts. RESULTS: HPLC-PDA-MSn analysis revealed caffeoylmalic acid as the major compound, followed by an acetyl-p-coumaroyl hexoside, puerol A, protocatechuic acid hexoside, ferulic acid and isorhamnetin-O-dihexoside. The extract exhibited total phenolic content of 109.59 ± 1.39 mg GAE/g, and demonstrated antioxidant activity across the in vitro chemical assays employed (DPPH, ABTS and FRAP). The decoction evidenced a dose-dependent inhibition of NO production in macrophages (IC50 = 34.99 ± 0.16 μg/mL), without cell-damaging effects. In NIH/3T3 fibroblasts, the extract showed the highest wound closure at 10 μg/mL, whereas both lower and higher concentrations exhibited diminished effects. CONCLUSIONS: A. paucinervis leaf decoction results suggested antioxidant, anti-inflammatory and wound-healing activities, without cell-damaging effects, supporting its widespread traditional use in the treatment of skin lesions and underscoring its potential as a future therapeutic drug.

articles.title: Finger Citron Fruit Ameliorates Ovariectomy-Induced Postmenopausal Metabolic Syndrome Through Regulation of Lipogenesis and Ferroptosis-Related Alterations.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: In Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM), "Jianpi Liqi Huatan" (strengthening the spleen, regulating qi, and resolving phlegm) represents a traditional therapeutic strategy for managing obesity-associated metabolic disorders. According to TCM theory, postmenopausal MS is primarily associated with spleen deficiency, qi stagnation, and phlegm-dampness accumulation. Finger Citron Fruit (FCF), a representative Lingnan medicinal and edible herb and a core herb for Jianpi Liqi Huatan, The correspondence between the traditional properties of FCF and this TCM pathological framework provides an ethnopharmacological rationale for investigating its effects on postmenopausal metabolic dysfunction. AIM OF THE STUDY: To explore the metabolic effects and mechanisms of FCF in postmenopausal MS. MATERIALS AND METHODS: An ovariectomy (OVX)-induced mouse model, OA&PA-induced primary hepatocytes, and untargeted serum metabolomics were employed to evaluate the therapeutic effects and molecular mechanisms of FCF against postmenopausal MS. RESULTS: FCF significantly improved metabolic homeostasis by reducing body weight gain, dyslipidemia, hepatic steatosis, adipose tissue accumulation, and systemic inflammation, while increasing whole-body energy expenditure. Untargeted metabolomics revealed that FCF restored a candidate metabolite putatively annotated as indole-3-acetylglutamic acid. FCF improved hepatic steatosis in association with downregulation of SREBP-1c/ChREBP-related lipogenic signaling and restoration of GPX4 and SLC40A1 expression, thereby alleviating oxidative stress and lipid peroxidation. CONCLUSIONS: FCF ameliorated postmenopausal MS by suppressing hepatic lipogenesis and attenuating ferroptosis-related alterations. These findings provide metabolomic and molecular evidence supporting its traditional "Jianpi Liqi Huatan" functions and highlight its therapeutic potential for postmenopausal MS.

articles.title: Microcirculatory, micro-rheological, metabolic and histomorphological investigation of experimental mesoblastic nephroma in rats treated with Vincristine.
articles.abstract: The development of malignant tumors and their abnormal vasculature can lead to severe changes in tissue perfusion. In this pilot study, we aimed to investigate changes in renal microcirculation and parenchymal abnormalities without treatment and after Vincristine treatment in a rat model of mesenchymal mesoblastic nephroma (Ne/De) tumor cell implantation of rat origin, which closely resembles Wilms' tumor. On the 1st, 4th, and 9th post-operative days, blood samples were collected to test for hematological parameters, erythrocyte deformability, and aggregation. In the Vincristine-treated group the animals received 0.25 mg/kg Vincristine on four occasions. We monitored renal microcirculation, obtained positron emission tomography imaging, and measured the blood flow of the abdominal aorta and the bilateral renal artery and vein. The kidneys were removed for histological analysis at the end of experiment. Leukocyte and platelet count gradually decreased in the Vincristine-treated group during the follow-up period. A significant increase in erythrocyte aggregation was observed after tumor implantation, while this increase was much smaller with Vincristine administration. Erythrocyte deformability deteriorated significantly by day 9th after tumor implantation. In the Tumor-implanted group, we observed structural characteristics of the tumor tissue and a heterogeneous blood flow pattern compared to the contralateral healthy kidney. The tumor growth inhibitory effect of Vincristine was observed. Malignant renal tumors caused significant deterioration and heterogeneity in microcirculation, which may be partly a consequence of abnormal vasculature and partly of deteriorating micro-rheology. The model is similar to Wilms tumor and is suitable for investigating rapid tumorigenesis, tumor vasculature, and therapeutical agents.

articles.title: 10-gingerol potentiates paclitaxel efficacy in triple-negative breast cancer by remodeling gut microbiota and suppressing PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway.
articles.abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) remains a clinical challenge due to its aggressive nature and chemoresistance, particularly to first-line agents such as paclitaxel (PTX). 10-Gingerol (10-G), the main pungent constituent of ginger, has been shown to possess anti-tumor and chemosensitizing properties. However, the mechanisms by which it potentiates PTX efficacy in TNBC remain incompletely understood. We established a 4 T1 TNBC-bearing BALB/c mouse model to assess the in vivo therapeutic effect of 10-G combined with PTX. Multi-omics analyses integrating 16S rRNA gene sequencing and transcriptome sequencing were performed to characterize gut microbial remodeling and tumor transcriptomic alterations. Results showed that combination therapy significantly inhibited tumor growth and cell proliferation with favorable safety and remodeled the gut microbiota by enriching beneficial genera (Limosilactobacillus, Lactobacillus) and reducing potentially pathogenic genera (Enterocloster, Mucispirillum). Transcriptomic profiling revealed that the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway in tumor tissues following combination treatment was markedly suppressed. Mechanistic validation through molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and Western blotting confirmed that 10-G directly binds to PI3K, AKT, and mTOR, and that combination therapy significantly suppressed phosphorylation of PI3K, AKT, and mTOR in tumor tissues. Collectively, this study demonstrates that 10-G augments the anti-tumor efficacy of PTX in TNBC, and this potentiation is mechanistically linked to favorable gut microbiota remodeling and targeted inhibition of the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling axis, thereby positioning 10-G as a promising chemosensitizing adjuvant for TNBC therapy.

articles.title: Development of an in vitro chemical hazard screening method using human iPSCs with and without metabolic activation and application to chlorinated paraffins.
articles.abstract: There is a growing need for new approach methodologies (NAMs) to screen the hazard of the increasing number of untested chemicals. Human induced pluripotent stem cells (h-iPSCs) represent a promising resource for developing such NAMs, provided their low metabolic potency is addressed. Here, we developed a proof-of-concept in vitro NAM combining h-iPSCs with pooled human liver S9 fractions (h-iPSCs-S9) to enable chemical hazard screening both with and without metabolic activation. Chlorinated paraffins (CPs) are mixtures of emerging contaminants whose regulation was delayed due to the lack of human-relevant data, and their effects in human cells remain poorly understood. Therefore, we used h-iPSCs-S9 to evaluate the hazard of short-, medium-, and long-chain CPs at human exposure levels (1-1000 μg/L). Three endpoints were assessed: cell viability; oxidative stress; and gene expression related to DNA repair systems, the peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor alpha-nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (PPARα-Nrf2) axis, and xenobiotic metabolism-related nuclear receptors and cytochrome P450s. Following validation, h-iPSCs-S9 showed responses consistent with several CP-associated effects observed in vivo and discerned the toxic effects of the three congener groups. Three hypotheses were proposed, where CPs might (1) alter human DNA repair and promote damage tolerance, (2) induce oxidative stress by suppressing PPARα-Nrf2 signaling through antagonism, and (3) act as weak antagonists, rather than agonists, of human xenobiotic metabolism. Overall, this study presents h-iPSCs-S9 as a reproducible and scalable NAM fit for chemical hazard screening, and calls for further investigation of the toxic modes of action of CPs in human cells.

articles.title: The impacts of polystyrene nanoplastics on colorectal cancer: Evidence from integrated network toxicity and in vitro approaches.
articles.abstract: Environmental ingestion of polystyrene nanoplastics (PNPLs) raises critical public health concerns, yet their impacts on colorectal cancer (CRC) remain obscure. In this study, network toxicology, and in vitro validation were integrated to evaluate the molecular mechanisms linking PNPLs to CRC. We identified 154 overlapping targets by integrating GEO-derived differentially expressed genes with PNPLs-predicted targets and CRC-associated genes, which are enriched in pathways associated with cancer signaling, apoptosis, oxidative stress, and inflammation. Using protein-protein interaction network, along with two machine learning algorithms (LASSO and Random Forest), we identified seven hub genes in which the expression of these genes was corroborated by the CRC database of TCGA, the CRC dataset of GEO, and the RT-qPCR analysis on HCT-116 cells. Molecular docking demonstrated the significant binding affinities between PNPLs and six hub targets. In vitro experiments with HCT-116 cells revealed PNPLs dose- and time-dependent cytotoxicity. Additionally, PNPLs induced oxidative stress by significant reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, collapse of mitochondrial membrane potential, and decrease of SOD, GPx and CAT activity. Furthermore, PNPLs caused apoptosis while concurrently pronounced pro-inflammatory responses by exciting the release of pro-inflammatory cytokines and mediators, including IL-6, IL-1β, TNF-α, NO, and PGE2. This study suggests the complex toxicity effects of PNPLs on CRC and supports the need for further research into nanoplastics as a potential environmental risk factor for CRC.

articles.title: Morin mitigates doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity via suppression of oxidative stress, inflammation, and structural remodeling.
articles.abstract: The clinical use of the anticancer drug doxorubicin is restricted by its ability to cause cardiotoxicity, often progressing to heart failure. Current cardiovascular treatments fail to restore cardiac function or improve long-term survival rates, demanding alternative therapeutic approaches to minimize the cardiotoxicity of conventional cancer treatments. Thus, this study investigated the alleviating potential of morin, a flavonoid with known cardioprotective, antioxidant, and anti-inflammatory effects, against doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity at two different time points. Sixty male Wistar rats were used in this study, which was divided into concurrent and post-treatment phases, each including normal, morin, doxorubicin, and morin-treated doxorubicin groups. Cardiotoxicity was induced by six intraperitoneal injections of doxorubicin (2.5 mg/kg every 48 h), while morin (50 mg/kg) was administered orally either concurrent (post-initial doxorubicin injection) or post-treatment (after all doxorubicin injections) for 12 days. Assessment included echocardiography and Doppler imaging to assess cardiac function, as well as biochemical, histological, morphometric, and immuno-histochemical analyses. Administration of morin mitigated doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity by reversing structural damage, reducing fibrosis, and improving heart function. This was accompanied by increased total antioxidant capacity and reduced levels of malondialdehyde and creatine kinase-MB, as well as suppressed tumor necrosis factor-alpha, interleukin-6, and cleaved-caspase-3 expressions in cardiac tissue. In conclusion, morin demonstrates notable efficacy against doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity by mitigating oxidative stress, inflammation, and structural remodeling. Consequently, morin represents a viable pharmacological candidate that merits clinical exploration to avert heart failure progression during doxorubicin chemotherapy.

articles.title: CAGE ionic liquid-mediated co-solubilization of lapatinib and resveratrol enhances cytotoxicity in lung cancer cells with uniform aerosolization for pulmonary delivery.
articles.abstract: Choline and geranic acid-based ionic liquids (CAGE-IL) have emerged as powerful delivery vehicles for many challenging drug molecules via different routes of administration. However, their potential for aerosol delivery has not been reported. In this study, CAGE-IL is investigated for its ability to solubilise a combination of lapatinib ditosylate (LPT) and resveratrol (RSV) as a potential vehicle for localised delivery in lung cancer therapy. The results showed that CAGE-IL had much higher solubility for LPT (114.6 ± 3.5 mg/mL vs. 0.02 mg/mL) and RSV (58.1 ± 6.8 mg/mL vs. 0.03 mg/mL) than their respective aqueous solubilities, as determined using a validated HPLC method developed for the simultaneous estimation of the molecules. An octanol/water partition coefficient of 2.34 for LPT from LPT-CAGE-IL and 2.18 for RSV from RSV-CAGE-IL was obtained. Upon evaluation in A549, a lung adenocarcinoma cell line, the IC50 value of LPT+RSV-co-loaded CAGE-IL was significantly lower (1.2 times, p˂0.006) than LPT solution (5.3 times, p˂0.0001) or RSV solution (2.7 times, p˂0.001). Importantly, we performed the first nebulization efficiency characterisation for CAGE-IL, obtaining 48 ± 1% for LPT and 49 ± 1% for RSV, with drug output rates of 15 mg/min for LPT and 7 mg/min for RSV and D50 of 2.74 µm. The MMAD, FPF, and GSD were 2.00 ± 0.2 µm, 74 ± 5 %, and 2.48 ± 0.2 for RSV, and 2.10 ± 0.3 µm, 70 ± 7 %, and 2.87 ± 0.2 for LPT showing the suitability of the prepared formulation for pulmonary use. Overall, achieving high solubility of both drugs in a single medium, along with near-identical recovery, signified uniform co-aerosolisation without phase separation during nebulization, indicating CAGE-IL as a possible vehicle for inhalation delivery, and enhance the therapeutic efficacy for localised lung cancer treatment.

articles.title: Composition-dependent changes in the crystallization mechanism in drug-drug coamorphous systems of related neuropeptide Y Y5 receptor antagonists.
articles.abstract: This study investigated the stabilization mechanisms of coamorphous systems using the related neuropeptide Y Y5 receptor antagonists NPY(A) and NPY(B). Physical mixtures (PMs) formed a eutectic mixture at an equimolar ratio. Thermal analysis during melting-cooling showed a single glass transition temperature (Tg) for each drug and the PMs, indicating amorphization of the individual drugs and coamorphization of NPY(A)-NPY(B). The Tg of NPY(A) was higher than that of NPY(B). Annealing at 15-17°C below Tg increased the Tg of all samples through structural relaxation. However, the τβ values obtained from both the Kohlrausch-Williams-Watts equation and ΔTg did not increase after coamorphization. Annealing promoted nucleation and accelerated crystallization of NPY(A), but not NPY(B). These phenomena were also observed in the coamorphous systems, suggesting composition-dependent crystallization mechanisms. Infrared spectroscopy revealed weak intermolecular interactions in the coamorphous systems. Isothermal crystallization tests showed that NPY(A)-rich and NPY(B)-rich coamorphous systems were stabilized by Tg elevation and nucleation inhibition, respectively. Spray-dried coamorphous systems exhibited improved stability and enhanced dissolution of both drugs in pH 6.8 phosphate buffer.

articles.title: A hybrid computational-analytical model for the prediction of stopper displacement in drug product prefilled syringe.
articles.abstract: Controlling the displacement of the plunger stopper within prefilled syringes (PFS) during air transportation is critical to maintain the sterility of the drug prod product. The presented computational-analytical hybrid model predicts stopper displacement during transportation at elevated altitude by integrating multi-physics principles including Newton's second law of motion, the ideal gas law, solid mechanics and Monte Carlo Simulations The hybrid model comprises four key components: stopper displacement prediction, manufacturing metric prediction, sensitivity study of input parameters, and design optimization. Model validation was performed against empirical experimental data from five PFS container closure configurations, demonstrating predictive accuracy with errors less than ±5%. The sensitivity study of the simulation model concludes that the stopper initial position, syringe barrel ID, filling volume, stopper rib OD and PFS syringe length are the top five parameters contributing to the stopper displacement. The design optimization function of the simulation model has been demonstrated through an example of optimizing the stopper initial position and fill volume to achieve the pre-defined stopper displacement. This work establishes a simulation model for predicting the stopper displacement of a PFS during air transportation, optimizing PFS container closure system design, fill and finish manufacturing process and ensuring reliable performance during transportation, with potential implications for improving drug product safety and delivery efficiency.

articles.title: Molecular weight-dependent properties of ciprofloxacin-loaded chitosan films: An in-vitro comparative study toward localized drug delivery for wound healing.
articles.abstract: Targeted or localized delivery to wounds is essential to avoid unwanted systemic effects of antibiotics. Ciprofloxacin hydrochloride (CH) is a broad-spectrum fluoroquinolone antibiotic used to treat skin and soft tissue infections. In this study, polymeric films were prepared by solvent casting using different molecular weights of chitosan (CT) and suitable plasticizers, such as propylene glycol (PG) or glycerin (GLY), to investigate their physicochemical properties, antimicrobial efficacy, drug release behavior, and stability. Polymer chain length and plasticizer selection influenced the films' physicochemical properties. The SEM, FTIR, DSC, XRD, and contact angle measurements revealed the transformation of the crystalline drug into an amorphous state, accompanied by hydrogen bonding between the drug and the polymer. The films demonstrated significant antibacterial efficacy and effective quantitative antimicrobial and antibiofilm profiling against some clinically relevant Gram-negative and Gram-positive bacteria. The initial drug release was also affected by the polymer's molecular weight; however, a complete release was noted within about 2 hours. The films fit the zero-order model better, followed by the Higuchi and Korsmeyer-Peppas models. The Korsmeyer-Peppas release exponent (n) values showed a correlation between CH release behavior from films and multiple independent physical parameters, establishing a predictive structure-property-release framework. The drug and excipients were compatible with each other and with the aluminum packaging, with no detectable chemical degradation, for at least 6 months under both accelerated and real conditions using the employed method. Such tunability underscores the adaptability of CT-based films as promising pre-formulation candidates that require further biological evaluation for localized therapeutic applications, where targeted drug delivery and rapid antimicrobial effects are paramount.

articles.title: Integrated gastric to intestinal pH-shift dissolution and permeation testing can predict the marked oral absorption enhancement of an itraconazole-carboxymethyl ethylcellulose amorphous solid dispersion.
articles.abstract: In this study, we aimed to investigate correlation of oral absorption and dissolution-permeation behaviors carboxymethyl ethylcellulose (CMEC)-based amorphous solid dispersion (ASD) for itraconazole (ITZ). Amorphization of ITZ and formation of the ASDs through ball milling were confirmed by powder X-ray diffraction, thermal and spectroscopic analyses, using hydroxypropyl methylcellulose acetate succinate (HPMCAS) as an additional carrier. ITZ rapidly dissolved in pH 1.2 medium; however, this was suppressed by ASD formation. The dissolution of ITZ in pH 6.8 medium was <0.2 μg/mL, which was improved by ASD formation. The ASD of ITZ-CMEC (3:7) especially enhanced dissolution to >15-fold that of HPMCAS-based ASDs. The drug-rich colloids generated and grew in the supersaturated solution, but they were effectively inhibited by CMEC. In the oral administration of the ASDs to rat, CMEC resulted in 2-fold higher area under the plasma concentration curve than HPMCAS. Additional dissolution studies combined with gastric, intestinal, and permeated compartments were performed. Both ASDs showed similar dissolution profiles in the simulated gastric fluid followed by reduction and re-dissolution in the fasted state gastrointestinal fluid. Approximately 2- and 1.5-fold higher dissolution and permeation by CMEC compared to HPMCAS was confirmed, respectively, reflecting oral absorption. Therefore, we conclude that CMEC is one of the best ASD carriers, and the oral absorption performances could be understood from the dissolution-permeation performances through both the gastric and intestinal phases.

articles.title: Investigation for the cause of vial breakage during frozen storage of nucleic acid drug solution and the effect of the internal coating on the vial strain.
articles.abstract: Vial breakage has been observed in nucleic acid drug solutions after deep-freezer storage, representing a critical quality concern in pharmaceutical manufacturing. This study aimed to investigate the cause underlying this phenomenon. Visual observation of reference vials revealed the "plugging off" phenomenon, defined as the instantaneous separation of the frozen drug matrix from the vial inner surface, which simultaneously induced vial breakage. Differential scanning calorimetry showed no crystallization peak during the freeze-thaw cycles, indicating that crystallization was not the cause. The thermomechanical analysis revealed that the frozen drug solution underwent volumetric contraction during freezing. Strain-gauge measurements further confirmed that significant mechanical strain developed in the vial wall concurrently with the "plugging off." Collectively, these findings provide a cause explanation for vial breakage in nucleic acid drug formulations, wherein the volumetric contraction of the frozen matrix compared to glass vial generates sufficient mechanical stress to fracture the vial. Additionally, an internal hydrophobic or silicone coating of the vial significantly influenced both the temperature at "plugging off" and suppressed the magnitude of the induced strain, protecting against breakage. This suggested that selecting an appropriate internal coating of the vial could represent one potential strategy for mitigating vial breakage.

articles.title: Nrf2 exerts an unfavorable role in chemical hepatotoxicity in mice by maintaining CYP2E1 protein stability.
articles.abstract: Nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2) is generally recognized for its protective role against chemical toxicity. However, in some cases the function of Nrf2 is not as expected. Using wild-type (WT) and Nrf2-knockout (Nrf2-KO) mice, we investigated the role of Nrf2 in hepatic injury induced by the typical hepatotoxicants, thioacetamide (TAA) and diethylnitrosamine (DEN). Both acute and chronic liver injury models were established. In the present study, Nrf2 deficiency was found to alleviate hepatic injury induced by TAA and DEN. Bioactivation of both TAA (reflected by its urinary oxidized metabolites and hepatic acetyllysine levels) and DEN (indicated by urinary acetaldehyde and hepatic O6-EtG levels) was significantly decreased in Nrf2-KO mice. Nrf2 deficiency resulted in a decrease in protein levels as well as an accelerated protein degradation of CYP2E1, which is considered the major enzyme catalyzing bioactivation of these chemicals. The decrease in CYP2E1 protein levels was accompanied by a significant increase in ROS and heme levels in response to chemical challenge in Nrf2-KO primary hepatocytes. These effects were reversed by the ROS scavenger N-acetylcysteine and the heme inhibitor 4,6-dioxoheptanoic acid. Collectively, these results indicate that Nrf2 facilitates chemical bioactivation by maintaining the stability of CYP2E1. This effect is partially mediated by ROS and heme signaling. Nrf2 acts as a promoter in chemical-induced hepatic injury, especially CYP2E1-dependent toxicants (TAA and DEN).

articles.title: Digital light processing 3D-printed PEGDA microneedle patches for sustained transdermal carbamazepine delivery.
articles.abstract: Microneedles (MNs) have emerged as a promising platform for transdermal drug delivery by overcoming the barrier properties of the stratum corneum while minimizing pain and improving patient compliance. In this study, digital light processing (DLP) three-dimensional printing was employed to fabricate PEGDA-based MN arrays for the controlled transdermal delivery of carbamazepine (CBZ). The influence of UV light intensity, layer exposure time, post-curing temperature and exposure time on the printability and mechanical properties of printed PEGDA and PEGDA/PEG 200 formulations was systematically investigated to identify optimal fabrication and post-curing conditions. Mechanical characterization demonstrated that curing at 50 °C for 45 min provided the most favourable balance between compressive modulus and ultimate strength for the PEGDA formulation. Three MN designs with different needle geometries and densities were fabricated and evaluated. The 300 and 300 MT designs exhibited significantly greater fracture resistance than the 200 μm design and possessed margins of safety exceeding unity, confirming their suitability for skin insertion. Ex-vivo porcine skin studies demonstrated successful penetration without structural deformation, while SEM analysis confirmed preservation of needle integrity following insertion. Drug incorporation reduced mechanical strength however did not compromise insertion performance. Both MN designs achieved sustained CBZ release over the experimental period, with release kinetics influenced by needle density and polymer composition. Cytocompatibility studies using HaCaT keratinocytes demonstrated good biocompatibility of the post-cured materials, whereas uncured resins exhibited pronounced cytotoxicity. Overall, the results demonstrate that DLP-fabricated PEGDA/PEG 200 MNs possess adequate mechanical robustness, controlled drug delivery capability, and favourable cytocompatibility, highlighting their potential as customizable platforms for sustained transdermal drug delivery.

articles.title: Clearance and retention of leachables in ultrafiltration and diafiltration applications.
articles.abstract: Ultrafiltration/diafiltration (UF/DF) operations are used to clear a broad range of process equipment-related leachables (PERLs) from process streams. While previous UF/DF studies have demonstrated efficient clearance by dilution and permeate removal, the contribution of adsorption to and retention within process-contact materials has remained largely unexplored. This study comprehensively investigated the clearance and retention of representative PERLs during UF/DF, referred to here as the "fate of leachables" concept. Controlled spiking experiments and adsorption studies were combined with extraction-based mass balances and kinetic modelling. Hydrophilic compounds behaved close to theoretical expectations and were efficiently removed via the permeate stream. In contrast, hydrophobic PERLs showed non-ideal clearance behaviour due to adsorption to contact materials, such as silicone tubing and polyethersulfone membranes, migration into polymer phases, and protein association. Most compounds were recovered by organic extraction, suggesting predominantly reversible surface adsorption, whereas DtBP showed incomplete recovery, indicating stronger system retention and/or migration into polymer phases. A source-sink model adapted from the Bateman equation successfully described the observed concentration profiles. These findings extend existing UF/DF clearance concepts by identifying process-contact materials as active sinks for PERLs and provide a mechanistic framework for more realistic prediction of PERL fate and interpretation of extractables and leachables data under manufacturing-relevant conditions.

articles.title: Liposome decoration via aminoalkyl nitrobenzene molecular gate triggers hypoxia-responsive cargo release.
articles.abstract: Although numerous anticancer agents are currently available, many still suffer from poor selectivity, resistance, tumor recurrence, and severe side effects. Liposomes have emerged as promising nanocarriers for anticancer drugs due to their biocompatibility and ability to be functionalized for selective release in the tumor microenvironment. In this study, hypoxia-responsive liposomes (HR-LPs) were designed by incorporating a novel molecular gate (MG) capable of contributing to disrupting the lipid bilayer under hypoxic conditions. This MG was integrated at different concentrations (10%, 15% and 20%) in the bilayer structure of liposomes loaded with a model molecule. These HR-LPs were synthesized using the thin-film hydration method and characterized in terms of size, polydispersity index, surface charge, and entrapment efficiency, providing optimal properties for drug delivery purposes. In vitro release studies were conducted using a Franz-diffusion cell setup under both normoxia and hypoxia conditions. Among the different formulations, only 15% HR-LPs showed a selective response to hypoxic conditions, with a significantly higher release rate and greater total amount of cargo released in the presence of nitroreductase (NTR), an enzyme overexpressed under hypoxic conditions, whereas conventional liposomes (CLPs) showed no significant differences between the tested conditions. Kinetic modelling indicated that cargo release involved both passive diffusion and relaxation processes, with MG incorporation increasing the contribution of the latter. These findings validate the developed manufacturing method and highlight 15% HR-LPs as a promising platform for further in vivo studies with antitumor agents, aiming to achieve controlled and targeted drug delivery in hypoxia-associated tumor environments.

articles.title: Curcumin-loaded lipid nanoparticles for photodynamic therapy in the topical treatment of melanoma.
articles.abstract: Melanoma remains one of the deadliest skin cancers, and current therapies still struggle to combine efficacy with minimal invasiveness. Photodynamic therapy (PDT) is a promising alternative, yet its translation is hindered by poor photosensitizer (PS) solubility and difficulty achieving effective localized skin delivery. This study developed multifunctional curcumin (Cur)-loaded solid lipid nanoparticles (Cur-SLN) and nanostructured lipid carriers (Cur-NLC) for topical PDT, incorporating lauric acid in both formulations and,in Cur-NLC, menthol to provide complementary functional properties to the lipid-based delivery system. Physicochemical characterization revealed mean particle sizes of 209 ± 4 nm (Cur-SLN) and 226 ± 9 nm (Cur-NLC), polydispersity indices below 0.3, negative surface charges of approximately - 20 mV, and high encapsulation efficiencies (76-78%). Both formulations demonstrated good stability and sustained Cur release. Franz diffusion studies using porcine skin showed no detectable Cur in the receptor compartment after 24 h, indicating negligible transdermal permeation. In vitro studies in L929 fibroblasts, HaCaT keratinocytes, and A375 melanoma cells showed a cytocompatible profile (≥70% viability) under non-irradiated conditions, while Cur-SLN and Cur-NLC reduced melanoma cell viability to < 15% upon blue light irradiation (420 nm), with PDT-mediated melanoma cell killing comparable to free Cur. Confocal microscopy showed a higher intracellular Cur-associated fluorescence signal in cells treated with Cur-NLC than in cells treated with Cur-SLN. Overall, Cur-loaded lipid nanoparticles demonstrated favourable physicochemical properties, sustained Cur release, good cytocompatibility, and strong PDT activity against melanoma cells, supporting their potential as topical PDT formulations with negligible transdermal permeation.

articles.title: Development and characterization of ultrasound-activated polymeric microdroplets for targeted chemotherapy.
articles.abstract: Potent antineoplastic agents such as afatinib and freebase doxorubicin exhibit promising antitumor activity but are limited by systemic toxicity, poor aqueous solubility, and restricted delivery to brain tumors. Here, we developed a co-evaporation synthesis strategy that extends a previously validated ultrasound-responsive methoxy poly(ethylene glycol)-poly(D,L-lactide) (mPEG-PDLLA) diblock copolymer-based carrier platform to efficiently encapsulate highly hydrophobic antineoplastic agents while preserving pressure-dependent, ultrasound-triggered drug release within a 300 kHz focused-ultrasound field. The resulting microdroplets are designed to serve as intravascular drug depots that retain their payload in the absence of ultrasound and release it on demand at the ultrasound focus, with the fraction released governed by the applied acoustic pressure. The polymeric microdroplets achieved encapsulation efficiencies of 39.6% for afatinib and 46.6% for doxorubicin. Both drugs exhibited reproducible pressure-dependent release; simultaneous logistic fitting with a shared transition-width parameter yielded half-maximal release pressures (P50) of 0.71 MPa for afatinib and 0.63 MPa for doxorubicin. Together, these findings establish a platform for localized, ultrasound-mediated release of highly hydrophobic antineoplastics and provide a foundation for future translational development toward targeted chemotherapy.

articles.title: Tunneling effect with time-dependent effective potential barrier: A semiclassical (WKB) reinterpretation of drug release kinetics in polymeric nanocapsules.
articles.abstract: Recent models describe drug release from polymeric nanoparticles through an analogy with quantum tunnelling, treating the delivery system as an effective rectangular potential barrier. The present work does not claim that quantum tunnelling has been experimentally established as the microscopic mechanism of drug permeation, nor that classical partition/diffusion models are generally inadequate. Rather, it reassesses whether the barrier formalism introduced in the pharmaceutical literature can be formulated with a physically motivated time dependence. In this work, we argue that this analogy is structurally identical to the standard solution of the Schrödinger equation for a rectangular barrier, and that the introduction of a multifractal formalism to describe time evolution - obtained via a formal Wick rotation (x→t) - lacks direct physical justification. We propose, instead, to treat the barrier height as an effective function of time, Ueff(t)=U0f(t), with f(t) varying slowly within the barrier region, reflecting the progressive degradation/swelling of the polymeric matrix, under two hypotheses for f(t) - exponential decay and rational decay (Hill-type). Rather than the thick-barrier WKB approximation, the exact transmission formula is used throughout, which is real-analytic in f(t) and continues smoothly into the resonance (over-barrier) regime once the barrier collapses, avoiding the artificial step-like transitions that a thick-barrier WKB treatment would produce near the collapse point.
